name: Marxist humanism
summary: Marxist humanism reads Marx through his early writings on alienation, treating socialism as the overcoming of estrangement so that people regain control of their own creative activity. It stresses human agency, ethics and praxis against economic determinism and Soviet dialectical materialism, and rejects Stalinism, vanguard-party rule and state capitalism in favor of workers' self-management and participatory democracy. It remains anti-capitalist, critical of consumerism and of private property as self-estrangement.
scope: The current of Marxist thought that reads Marx through his early writings on alienation and makes human agency, subjectivity and ethics central, as the sources describe it: the humanist reading dated from Fromm's Marx's Concept of Man (1961) and the 1844 Manuscripts; the 1965 Fromm symposium Socialist Humanism and its Western, Eastern-European and Third-World contributors; Raya Dunayevskaya's Marxist-Humanism; the Yugoslav Praxis group (Petrovic, Markovic), and the Czech and Polish dissident humanists such as Kosik. The sources set it against the 'objectivist' orthodox historical materialism of Stalin's Soviet Union and against Althusser's structuralist Marxism. It does not take in Leninist or Althusserian readings, and the sources do not make the whole Frankfurt School or the British New Left part of it: they count only individual contributors (Fromm, Marcuse's symposium essay).
